clue.text: Church member taking professional exam sitting by a social worker

indicators.note: one piece sits right beside the next, so the parts are placed side by side

parts.note: a pro is short for a professional
a test is an examination
the ant is the classic social insect and a worker in its colony

explanation.surface: A churchgoer takes a professional qualification exam while sitting beside someone from social services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a council employee, but it is the crossword ant, a worker insect living in a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A Protestant belongs to one of the Western churches that broke from Rome at the Reformation.

clue.text: None for bad cover

indicators.note: bad letters are corrupted ones, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means none

explanation.surface: Nothing is offered in place of poor insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'None' gives O; 'bad' rearranges O plus FOR into ROOF.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof is the covering on top of a building.

clue.text: A flier's given a little dainty morsel

parts.note: a tit is a small bird, a flier
a bit is a little

explanation.surface: A bird gets given a small bit of tasty food.
explanation.definitionFit: A titbit is a small tasty piece of food, a delicacy.

clue.text: Pretended to have a couple of thousand in store

indicators.note: one piece placed in the other, so the thousands go inside the store

parts.note: a shed is a storage hut
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two are MM

explanation.surface: Someone claimed falsely to have two thousand saved up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'store' looks like a shop or savings, but is a verb-like noun for a storage hut; 'to have' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Shammed means faked or feigned, putting on a false show.

clue.text: Opposite to a tin works

indicators.note: letters that are worked are reshaped and rearranged

explanation.surface: Facing a tin factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Being anti something means being against or opposed to it.

clue.text: The beast turning about is a renegade

indicators.note: turning the whole string round means reading these pieces backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written
a rat is a deserter or traitor

explanation.surface: An animal that turns around proves to be a deserter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the whole of RE + IS + RAT (REISRAT), giving TARSIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarsier is a small big-eyed primate of Southeast Asian forests, an animal.

clue.text: Wet conditions impair lustre of craft

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or impair
shine is gloss or lustre
SS stands for steamship, a craft

explanation.surface: Damp weather spoils the polish on boats.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshiness is the state of being boggy, waterlogged ground.

clue.text: A skilled worker means son to get moving!

indicators.note: letters made to get moving shift about into a new order

explanation.surface: A craftsman tells his son to hurry up.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason is a craftsman who cuts and lays stone.

clue.text: Strict diet with rapid results

explanation.surface: A severe diet that promises quick weight loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Going without food is a fast, and something quick or speedy is also fast.

clue.text: Businessman finding it's cold riding a farmer's vehicle

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
riding on something means being on it
a tractor is the vehicle a farmer drives across the fields

explanation.surface: A businessman feels the chill while perched on a farm tractor.
explanation.definitionFit: A contractor is a self-employed tradesman or firm hired to do jobs, a kind of businessman.

clue.text: Waters on time

parts.note: the seas are bodies of water
taken as written

explanation.surface: Water flows over the clock face, or a tide comes in on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A season is a period of the year, such as the holiday or football time.

clue.text: Creating dreadful to-do, he's appeased

indicators.note: making something dreadful out of the letters means they are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: After causing a terrible fuss, a man is finally placated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creating dreadful' tells you to rework the letters of TO-DO HE'S (TODOHES) into SOOTHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Soothed and appeased both describe someone calmed and pacified after anger.

clue.text: Deciding not to compete but chafing

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws from a race because of rubbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Scratching is withdrawing from a contest, and it is also rubbing or itching the skin.

clue.text: No Government can be long secure without a formidable Disraeli (Coningsby)

definitions.text: No Government can be long secure without a formidable Disraeli (Coningsby)

parts.words: No Government can be long secure without a formidable Disraeli (Coningsby)
parts.note: a quotation from Disraeli's novel Coningsby with its last word missing; the missing word is the party facing the government

explanation.surface: A quotation from Benjamin Disraeli's novel Coningsby about government needing a strong rival.
explanation.walkthrough: The full quotation ends 'a formidable Opposition': fill in the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The Opposition is the main party not in power, which challenges the governing party.

clue.text: Bearing in some animals, administers medication

indicators.note: one piece placed inside the other, so the bearing goes into the animals

parts.note: does are female deer
S, south, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A vet with a calm manner treats a group of creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' means a compass direction here, giving S.
explanation.definitionFit: Doses means gives someone measured amounts of a drug.

clue.text: The down-to earth view as one's entering a country

indicators.note: one piece goes into another, so the letters for one's are placed inside

parts.note: a realm is a kingdom, a country under a monarch
one's is one + is, giving I (Roman one) and S, read as IS

explanation.surface: A practical outlook, seen as someone arrives in a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', giving I + S; these go into REALM between L and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism is a practical attitude that accepts things as they are, a down-to-earth outlook.

clue.text: Circular French article in cane

indicators.note: one piece placed inside another, so the article goes into the cane

parts.note: a rod is a stick or cane
un is the French for a

explanation.surface: A round French item made of wicker.
explanation.definitionFit: Round and circular both describe the shape of a ring.

clue.text: A fellow with gold is an open handed individual

parts.note: a don is a university fellow or lecturer
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A rich man with gold bullion turns out to be generous.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldry term for gold, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives money or goods freely, so is generous with their gifts.

clue.text: Completely absorbed in a new part

indicators.note: a new version of the word part means its letters are given a fresh order

explanation.surface: An actor is utterly engrossed in a freshly cast role.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rapt means being wholly engrossed or captivated by something.

clue.text: Report presenting all the main points

parts.note: the four cardinal points of the compass are north, east, west and south
east, abbreviated E, is one of the cardinal points
west, abbreviated W, is one of the cardinal points
south, abbreviated S, is one of the cardinal points

explanation.surface: A summary giving every key point of a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main points' hints at a summary, but means the compass points N, E, W and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A report of recent events is information, such as what a bulletin carries.

clue.text: Red colouring in the kitchen — natural of course

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: A red dye made in the kitchen, naturally from plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish-brown dye from a shrub, used on hair and skin.

clue.text: The near-riotous rally

indicators.note: riotous letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A demonstration that almost turns into a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten is to encourage, to rally someone's spirits.

clue.text: Streets a painter will turn up to get a magazine

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reverses the whole string read upwards

parts.note: lanes are narrow streets
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A painter will appear on the streets to collect a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses LANES + RA together (LANESRA). 'magazine' means a store for weapons, not a periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a store for weapons and ammunition, which is what a magazine is.

clue.text: These may be infused and set as in moulds

indicators.note: moulding something reshapes it, so these letters take a new form

explanation.surface: Jellies that are steeped and then left to set in shapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moulds' looks like a noun for jelly shapes, but is a verb telling you to reshape SET AS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tisanes are herbal teas made by steeping leaves or flowers in hot water.

clue.text: Uses picture issue

parts.note: to draw is to picture something with pencil
issue means offspring, so a son

explanation.surface: Uses a picture as the basis for a printed issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' is the legal word for children, so SON.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw on a resource is to make use of it.

clue.text: Records of Western ceremonies

parts.note: rites are ceremonies

explanation.surface: Documents about Western rituals.
explanation.definitionFit: Writes means puts down in words, setting things down as a record.

clue.text: Beat her to get here

parts.note: to beat is to hit
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to strike a woman to make her come.
explanation.definitionFit: Hither is an old word meaning to this place, as in come here.

clue.text: Make an impression as a model

explanation.surface: A model makes an impact.
explanation.definitionFit: To type is to strike letters onto paper, and a type is also a pattern or example.

clue.text: He squashed lime

indicators.note: squashed fruit is crushed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man crushed a citrus fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Emil is a man's name, so it can stand for he.

clue.text: Judicial term for ordeal

parts.note: a court trying a case is acting judicially
a term is a period of time

explanation.surface: A legal word for a harrowing experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judicial term' looks like one phrase for legal jargon, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficult period of hardship is an ordeal.

clue.text: Recess if there's total lack to accord

parts.note: no means none at all
to OK something is to agree to it

explanation.surface: A space in the wall left empty because there is nothing to agree on.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small alcove or corner set back in a room.

clue.text: Unnecessarily irritates with cunning

parts.note: to needle someone is to annoy them
sly means crafty or cunning

explanation.surface: Someone annoys others craftily and for no good reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something needlessly means doing it without any need, without reason.
